physical_harm: Death of the new-born baby girl
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the evidence that the baby girl was placed in an incubator with an oxygen mask, did not open her eyes, and did not cry after birth, indicating a possibility of natural death.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the credibility of the witnesses, noting that the prosecution relied on circumstantial evidence and the statements of nurses PW-8 and PW-9, but found that the chain of circumstances was not sufficiently established to convict the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
bail_history: Appellant is on bail, her bail bonds stand cancelled
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 24 August 2007; Trial judgment: 19 December 2009; High Court decision: 12 March 2010; Supreme Court decision: 17 December 2019
legal_representation: Ms. Mahalakshmi Pavani, Sr. Adv., Ms. Shiva Vijay Kumar, Neeleshwar, Mrs. Rama, Mrs. Anjani Aiyagari, Advs. for the Appellant; Anmol Chandan, Pranay Ranjan, B. V. Balaram Das, Advs. for the Respondent
investigation_status: Case registered on 31 August 2007; Post-mortem conducted on 26 August 2007; Trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment; High Court: Confirmed conviction and sentence; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed, conviction set aside, appellant acquitted
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused caused the death of her newborn baby girl by strangulation, based on circumstantial evidence, and that the chain of circumstances was established to prove her guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the conviction was based solely on circumstantial evidence without establishing a complete chain of circumstances, and that there was a possibility of natural death of the child, making the evidence insufficient to convict the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that conviction cannot be based solely on circumstantial evidence unless a complete chain of circumstances is established to prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
